section_summary: This section follows U.S. policy on Japanese industrial reparations, production limits, shipping, and shipbuilding from 1947 to 1949. It also records British and Soviet reactions, reports rising Japanese industrial output, and examines competition, industrial rationalization, small businesses, and technical development. The section ends partway through a Japanese government “Technical White Paper.”

subfiles.title: Disposition of U.S. Share of Japanese Reparations
subfiles.about: Explains why private U.S. claims on Japanese industrial reparations were discouraged.
subfiles.summary: Commerce expected little private demand and administration costs exceeding likely sale proceeds; Clayton approved the recommendation.

subfiles.title: Waiver of U.S. Share in German and Japanese Industrial Assets Available as Reparations
subfiles.about: Recommends conditions for waiving U.S. claims to Japanese industrial assets.
subfiles.summary: Seeks approval to discuss German and Japanese reparations recommendations with affected agencies.

subfiles.title: Discrepancy Regarding ACA Plant No. 1602
subfiles.about: Clarifies the classification of Japanese plant numbers 1602 and 1488.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the listed plants are components of electric arc furnaces.

subfiles.title: Comment on Attached Draft Cable
subfiles.about: Discusses how SCAP should allocate divisible property sought by multiple countries.
subfiles.summary: Suggests deferring contested allocations while governments seek agreement on reparations shares.

subfiles.title: German Reparation and Dismantling
subfiles.about: Urges a Cabinet decision on German dismantling and deliveries to the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: Proposes seeking British and French agreement to suspend uncompensated deliveries.

subfiles.title: Senate Briefing on Reparations and Dismantling
subfiles.about: Plans briefing material for Senate consideration of German reparations and dismantling.
subfiles.summary: Saltzman anticipates executive sessions and floor debate, and prepares memoranda for State witnesses and Senator Vandenberg.

subfiles.title: Cabinet Discussion of Dismantling
subfiles.about: Relays notes from the January 23 Cabinet meeting on dismantling.
subfiles.summary: Royall supported a proposed procedure; Harriman and Krug opposed dismantling.

subfiles.title: Soviet Press on Japanese Industry Proposal
subfiles.about: Reports Soviet press criticism of votes against a Soviet Japanese industry proposal.
subfiles.summary: Quotes Ambassador Panyushkin's criticism of opposing powers.

subfiles.title: Statement Regarding Level of Economic Life in Japan
subfiles.about: Authorizes an interim statement on pending U.S. views of Japanese industry.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges other governments' concern and promises a U.S. position as soon as possible.

subfiles.title: Japanese Competition
subfiles.about: Transmits a British parliamentary answer on potential Japanese competition.
subfiles.summary: The answer promises consultation with industry and action against unfair, low wage competition.

subfiles.title: Japanese Prices for Textile Machinery: Patents in Japan
subfiles.about: Records U.S. industry concerns over Japanese patents, textile machinery prices, and a South American sales mission.
subfiles.summary: Mason feared copying and underpricing. McCornick described patent registration and SCAP floor price policy, and explained Pickelle's presence on the trade mission.

subfiles.title: Soviet Press Report on Japanese War Industry
subfiles.about: Reports Soviet accusations that the U.S. planned to rebuild Japanese war industry.
subfiles.summary: Cites claims about future steel output and MacArthur's reparations decisions.

subfiles.title: March Industrial Production Index
subfiles.about: Transmits a SCAP release on Japan's March industrial production.
subfiles.summary: Reports postwar highs in the overall index, coal, metals, chemicals, and textiles, alongside a machinery decline.

subfiles.title: Policy Regarding Japanese Industry
subfiles.about: Records a British Embassy request for a U.S. position on Japanese industry.
subfiles.summary: Graves pressed for a statement to the Far Eastern Commission. Allison connected the delay to reparations policy and anticipated talks with ambassadors.

subfiles.title: Policy Regarding Japanese Industry
subfiles.about: Expresses British concern over delayed U.S. instructions on Japanese industry.
subfiles.summary: Asks for progress on the pending Far Eastern Commission policy paper.

subfiles.title: April Industrial Production Index
subfiles.about: Transmits a SCAP release on Japan's April industrial production.
subfiles.summary: Reports a new postwar index high, with gains in metals, chemicals, machinery, and building materials.

subfiles.title: Japanese Level of Industry
subfiles.about: Forwards departmental views on Japanese industry, shipping, and shipbuilding.
subfiles.summary: Requests circulation of the attached policy material within GA.

subfiles.title: Japanese Level of Industry
subfiles.about: Explains proposed letters seeking defense views and addressing Japanese shipping policy.
subfiles.summary: Recommends approval of a letter on post occupation security limits and a response to an Army shipbuilding study.

subfiles.title: Japanese Level of Industry
subfiles.about: Presents a letter seeking military advice on Japanese industrial restrictions.
subfiles.summary: Highlights aircraft manufacturing, shipping, and shipbuilding.

subfiles.title: Proposed Letter on Post Occupation Industry Restrictions
subfiles.about: Requests military views on security restrictions for Japanese nonarmament industries.
subfiles.summary: The draft cites U.S. support for peaceful Japanese production while asking whether aircraft manufacturing and merchant shipping or shipbuilding need limits after occupation.

subfiles.title: Views on Japanese Shipping and Shipbuilding
subfiles.about: Comments on an Army study of Japanese merchant shipping and shipbuilding.
subfiles.summary: State supports rebuilding a Japanese merchant marine and ending further industrial reparations. The draft discusses ship construction, security limits, U.S. vessel charter restrictions, and competition with American shipping. It proposes developing policy with the Navy and Maritime Commission through the Shipping Coordinating Committee.

subfiles.title: Information on Japanese War Supporting Industries
subfiles.about: Seeks Army concurrence to provide industrial information to the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Proposes tabular answers to a New Zealand representative's questions.

subfiles.title: Proposed Reply to New Zealand Query
subfiles.about: Introduces tabular information requested by New Zealand.
subfiles.summary: The surviving OCR preserves only fragments of the proposed reply.

subfiles.title: New Industrial Indexes Developed
subfiles.about: Transmits a SCAP release explaining revised Japanese industrial indexes.
subfiles.summary: The new indexes use a 1932–1936 base, more production series, utilities, and value added weights. The release compares sector trends and identifies textiles as notably below the base period.

subfiles.title: Reply to New Zealand Representative's Information Request
subfiles.about: Proposes sending General McCoy information on Japanese war industries and reparations removals.
subfiles.summary: Encloses an instruction for the Commission's September meeting.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Reports on Certain Japanese Industries
subfiles.about: Forwards a SCAP response to French questions about selected Japanese industries.
subfiles.summary: Encloses figures on chemicals, carbons, colors, and fatty alcohols.

subfiles.title: Information About Japanese Industries
subfiles.about: Answers French inquiries on selected Japanese industrial products.
subfiles.summary: Provides prewar and current capacity, production, quality, and export information for hydrosulfites, electrical carbons, vitrifiable colors, and fatty alcohols.

subfiles.title: Enquiry Concerning the Japanese Industry of Cellulosic Films
subfiles.about: Requests data and samples concerning Japanese cellulosic film production.
subfiles.summary: Asks about plants, output, exports, imports, and samples.

subfiles.title: Machinery Industry and Deconcentration
subfiles.about: Requests views on whether Japanese industrial rationalization appears to conflict with deconcentration.
subfiles.summary: Citing Hiromu Higuchi, the Department asks whether the public confuses efficient production with concentrated ownership and suggests discussing any misunderstanding with SCAP.

subfiles.title: Replacement Record Copy Notice
subfiles.about: Identifies a replacement record copy of Tokyo despatch 770.
subfiles.summary: The original action copy had not been returned.

subfiles.title: Effect of Industrial Rationalization Program on Medium and Small Enterprises
subfiles.about: Reports SCAP views on rationalization and the survival of smaller Japanese firms.
subfiles.summary: SCAP officials describe a move away from direct plant selection toward gradual economic pressure. The mission warns that credit shortages and other disadvantages may eliminate viable small firms, allowing rationalization to undermine deconcentration.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Statement Regarding Small Business in Japan
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a SCAP bulletin on Japanese small business.
subfiles.summary: Highlights the Smaller Enterprises Agency's assistance to firms.

subfiles.title: Small Business in Japan
subfiles.about: Describes Japan's small firms and the Smaller Enterprises Agency.
subfiles.summary: The bulletin gives firm counts and describes agency advice, loans, training, consultation offices, and exhibitions. It predicts improvement while acknowledging difficult conditions for many firms.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Technical White Paper
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards and evaluates a Japanese government report on industrial technology.
subfiles.summary: The despatch outlines uneven Japanese technical capacity, weak quality control, low productivity, and dependence on copied foreign technology. It also summarizes newspaper responses calling for better techniques to support exports.

subfiles.title: A Basic Step
subfiles.about: Argues for investment in Japanese industrial research and technical skill.
subfiles.summary: The editorial treats technological progress as essential to higher quality exports and living standards. It urges shared research, consulting engineers, government support, and capital for inventions.

subfiles.title: Present Conditions of the Mining and Industrial Technics of Our Country
subfiles.from: Agency of Industrial Science and Technology, Ministry of International Trade and Industry
subfiles.about: Surveys Japan's mining and manufacturing techniques and their role in economic recovery.
subfiles.summary: A title page and detailed contents list cover resources, power, machinery, chemicals, textiles, research, patents, standards, and technical training. The opening text calls for greater public attention to technology and argues that improved productivity and quality are necessary for exports and economic stability. The document continues beyond page 316.
